title: Fihrids
capsule: The Fihrids were an Arab dynasty descended from Uqba ibn Nafi al-Fihri, founder of al-Qayrawan, who governed Ifriqiya (the al-Qayrawan heartland of modern Tunisia and Tripolitania) in the twilight of Umayyad and dawn of Abbasid rule. Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib al-Fihri seized control of the province in 745 and ruled it as a virtually autonomous emir until 755, navigating the Umayyad collapse and the Abbasid takeover from the Maghrib's distant western frontier. A bloody family quarrel after his death threw Ifriqiya into chaos, and his son Habib's brief rule (755–757) ended when the Fihrid line was overrun and extinguished in a Kharijite Berber uprising in 757–758. (A separate Fihrid, Yusuf ibn Abd al-Rahman, simultaneously ruled al-Andalus until Abd al-Rahman I deposed him in 756.)
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Fihrid territorial extent is reasonably well attested for al-Andalus through Arabic chronicles; their precise administrative boundaries within the peninsula are not mapped in detail by modern scholarship.
